## Overview {#overview}

Students train models and deploy them on microcontrollers, where limits on
memory, energy, and latency shape every design choice. This page
collects the materials from the Harvard CS249r offerings and the HarvardX TinyML
program. The course assumes Python and basic linear algebra.

## Syllabus and schedule {#syllabus}

The [TinyML syllabus](https://mlsysbook.ai/instructors/tinyml-syllabus.html)
pairs each week of the courseware with a Volume I chapter. The syllabi of past
Harvard offerings appear under [Offerings](#offerings).

## Materials {#materials}

| Resource | Use |
|:---|:---|
| [Lecture slides](https://mlsysbook.ai/slides/tinyml.html) | Decks from the HarvardX TinyML courseware. |
| [Hardware kits](https://mlsysbook.ai/kits/) | Microcontroller boards and deployment labs. |
| [Fall 2020 assignments](https://github.com/Harvard-CS249R-Fall2020/assignments) | Starters for hello world, gesture recognition, person detection, wake words, and responsible AI. |
| [Fall 2022 Assignment 2](https://github.com/mmaz/cs249r-a2) | Visual wake words: training, quantization, and deployment ([Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/mmaz/cs249r-a2/blob/master/cs249r_a2.ipynb)). |
| [TinyMLx courseware](https://github.com/tinyMLx/courseware/tree/master/edX) and [Colabs](https://github.com/tinyMLx/colabs) | Structure, readings, and notebooks from the HarvardX specialization. |
| [TinyMLx Arduino library](https://github.com/tinyMLx/arduino-library) | Source and examples for the TinyML kit and shield. |

## For instructors {#for-instructors}

The historical code and hardware instructions have not been rerun on current
toolchains, so each assignment needs a test run before it is assigned.

Project showcases from
[2023](https://sites.google.com/g.harvard.edu/cs249-tinyml-2023/fall-2023-final-projects)
and [2022](https://sites.google.com/g.harvard.edu/cs249-tinyml-2023/fall-2022-final-projects)
remain on the original course site. Selected projects with public code:

- [Cache 4 Trash](https://github.com/AditiR-42/cache-4-trash): waste sorting with
  a Nicla Vision classifier and a motorized sorter.
- [Activity recognition and ultrasound power control](https://github.com/euranofshin/ultrasound-power-tinyml):
  activity recognition on a Nicla Vision that controls ultrasound power.
- [Air Guitar](https://github.com/RobJMal/Air-Guitar-CS249R): gesture
  recognition from motion and finger-flex sensors on a Teensy board.

The [course directory](../index.qmd) lists TinyML courses at other institutions.
